- 菜单、手机首页菜单、最近、收藏、首页「最近访问」现在用同一条规则：和某个对象有关的条目（对象本身、它的列表视图、它的记录）画这个对象的彩色图标块；仪表盘、报表、页面、链接、动作等其他条目一律画浅灰底、深灰图标的中性块。颜色只表示「是哪个对象」。
- 原来最近/收藏里的表情符号去掉了，换成同样的图标块。分组标题和分隔线不变。
- 卡片第 4 项（对象自动取色）还在等维护者决定，所以 PR 写的是 Part of，卡片保持打开，这是对的。
- 没有发现必须改的问题。

None.

### Should-fix

None.

### Nits (ride or drop, seat's call)

- **N1** `contentItemTile.tsx` `CONTENT_KIND_ICON` repeats `NAV_KIND_ICON`'s glyphs for `dashboard` / `report` / `page` by hand; the comment says they are the menu's. Spreading the layout map (or reading `resolveNavKindIcon`) would keep the two from drifting when a glyph changes.
- **N2** `HomeRail.tsx` draws the object tile on `object || icon`. A row with an `icon` but no read `objectDef` still gets an object tile with `color` undefined (the tile's own default), which is what main did; with the new `object` flag the `|| icon` arm is only that fallback. Fine as is; worth a one-line comment if it rides.

- Card #36141 items 1–3, 5–7 against the diff; item 4 excluded and the PR says so (Part of).
- `NavigationRenderer`: non-object rows go `resolveNavKindIcon(item)` = `resolveNavItemIcon(item) ?? NAV_KIND_ICON[type]`; `NavIconTarget` is only `{ kind: 'object' }`, so no target icon was reachable on the non-object path before and none is lost. `object` / `group` / `separator` return `undefined` and keep their own paths. View entries are `type: 'object'` with `viewName`, so they take the object's tile (item 3).
- Action rows: `navIconClass` removed, the neutral tile drawn (md on mobile, sm otherwise), so the phone app home follows the same rule through `nav-menu-renderer` (item 7).
- `favoriteItemObject` parses `object:NAME`, `view:OBJECT:VIEW`, `record:OBJECT:ID` and refuses a prefix that does not match the type; Recent rows read `recentItemObject`; emoji removed (item 5/6).
- `NeutralIconTile` = private `IconTile` with `NEUTRAL_ICON_TILE_CLASS` (light and dark pairs, pinned by the test) and `data-neutral-icon-tile`; `ObjectIconTile` behaviour unchanged; both exported from `custom/index.ts`.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `eb36a39789d71df8bdd5a5c948d6e34fae449ac2`
Local-runs: none

Read: card #36141 (body and its three comments: the dispatch record 7065885381, triage 7065928977, the seat claim 7066071936), epic #34571 (body), `/mnt/project-files/build-seat1/36141/fable-decision.md` (context only), PR #36164 (body, 18-file list, the net diff `f5553525..eb36a397`, one commit), and the check-runs on the head. Every check-run on `eb36a397` is `success` or `skipped` (opt-in and queue-verdict jobs); none failed. Those include Check Changeset, Spec property liveness, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Type Check UI, Lint UI, Test UI 1-16, Build and E2E UI and Live E2E UI. Scope is items 1-3 and 5-7, as the claim says. Item 4 is held with the maintainer, so the PR says `Part of #36141`, which is right.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set: no change. No `packages/spec` path, schema, validator or `objectui validate` input is touched. `app.zod.ts` describes a nav item's `icon` only as "Icon name", with no fallback semantics, so drawing a kind glyph when none is authored contradicts no published text. Right.

Public surface (published d.ts):
- `@object-ui/components` adds `NeutralIconTile`, `NeutralIconTileProps` (`Omit` of `ObjectIconTileProps` minus `color`) and `NEUTRAL_ICON_TILE_CLASS`, through `custom/index.ts`. This is a pure widening, named right. `ObjectIconTile` keeps its signature and DOM: the same `data-object-icon-tile` value and the same class set. The body moved into a private `IconTile`, and the destructured `glyph` was renamed only inside the function.
- `@object-ui/layout` adds `NAV_KIND_ICON` and `resolveNavKindIcon`. Both reach the package entry through `export * from './NavigationRenderer'`. This is a pure widening, named right. The record's key type is `Exclude` of the item-type union minus `object`, `group` and `separator`, so a new kind added to the union fails type-check until it is given a glyph. That is good.
- Behaviour on an existing export: `NavigationRenderer` now draws every non-object leaf and action row on `NeutralIconTile`. Without an authored `icon`, such a row draws its kind's glyph instead of the generic one. The `nav:menu` block does the same. This is a visual default change with no API removed or renamed. Under ruling A it rides the widening at patch.
- `@object-ui/app-shell`: `ContentItemTile`, `favoriteItemObject` and `CONTENT_KIND_ICON` are module exports of `layout/contentItemTile.tsx`, which the package entry does not export, and the package is `private`. No public surface. The PR body's "not exported" is right.
- `RecentItemContext.object` (HomeRail) is a new optional field on a type internal to app-shell. Not public.
- Docs: `content/docs/frontend/layout.mdx` now describes the two tiles and `NAV_KIND_ICON`, which matches the code.

Code against the card's rule (colour says only which object a row is, and every row is one tile):
- Items 1 and 2: the leaf arm picks `ObjectIconTile` only for `object` plus `objectName`, and the action arm uses `NeutralIconTile` with `resolveNavKindIcon`. An authored `icon` still wins (`resolveNavKindIcon` goes through `resolveNavItemIcon` first). This is pinned by `NavigationRenderer.objectTile-35985.test.tsx` for all seven kinds, an action, and a row inside a group.
- Item 3: a `viewName` entry is still `type: 'object'`, so it takes the object arm. Pinned (`My accounts` draws orange).
- Item 5: the group heading and separator arms are untouched. Pinned.
- Item 6: the favourite ids the sidebar parses match their writers on the head: `object:NAME` (SidebarItemMenu), `view:OBJECT:VIEW` (`listViewFavoriteId`) and `record:OBJECT:ID` (RecordDetailView). The app favourite `app:NAME` that AppCard stores as `type: 'object'` is correctly not taken for an object, because the prefix check refuses it. Recent rows reuse `recentItemObject`. On Home, the object and view rows now read their object's icon and colour (the 12604 pins were flipped and say why). The emoji are gone, and the test pins that.
- Item 7: the phone home menu is the same `NavigationRenderer` at `md`. Evidence is in the 375 shots. It follows by construction.
- Contrast: the neutral tile is pinned at ≥ 4.5:1 in both themes. In the `after-sidebar-dark-1440` shot, the dark-theme tile reads clearly against the sidebar.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/36141-menu-icon-tiles.md` bumps `@object-ui/components`, `@object-ui/layout` and `@object-ui/app-shell` at `patch`. The diff publishes in exactly those three packages; app-shell is private but versioned, as `privatePackages.version: true` provides. Ruling A says the level follows the Metadata-protocol line. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: no spec text, default or meaning changes. With `Clause-②: yes (widening)` alone, that ships patch. Right.

`Clause-②: yes (widening)` appears on both the PR body and the changeset, and each names the same five added exports with nothing removed or renamed. That matches the d.ts delta above. Right. Check Changeset is green.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev flags in the PR body: item 4 is held out, with a follow-up if the maintainer chooses it, and HotCRM declares no object colour, so its object tiles are the grey palette square. Both are answered. They belong to the maintainer's decision card and to the card's own "not doing" list (HotCRM is changed elsewhere), not to this PR. The ordering against #36112 is stated on the claim. The PR carries no `open_questions` entries.

SQL push-down: there is no finding. The diff adds no data query, no id materialisation and no in-app join. Every new read is a metadata-cache read of object definitions by name, which has no SQL form. One adjacent read-shape point, inferred from reading the code and not measured, is listed under should-fix S1.

Must-fix: none.

Should-fix (none blocks this verdict):
- S1. The sidebar's Recent, Favorites and Starred tiles add by-name object reads with no presence gate. `contentTile` in `UnifiedSidebar.tsx` calls `ContentItemTile`, which calls `useNavTargetIcon` and `useNavTargetColor`, which call `readObjectsByName` with the names-only scope. Favourite rows and Recent record rows asked nothing before (they drew emoji). Now each object they name that is not already read is asked by name. That includes a favourite whose object's package was later disabled. Home deliberately does not ask such an object by name: per objectstack#34692, `readRecentObjects` makes one presence read through `?names=` and asks nothing by name for an `absent` or `unread` name. Either gate these rows the same way (one batched presence read for the names the rows carry, then draw the grey object tile with no by-name ask for an absent name), or give the reason in the PR. A follow-up commit or card is fine.

Nits:
- N1. `ui/packages/layout/src/NavigationRenderer.tsx`, lines 236 to 243, is the jsdoc of the public `NavIconTarget`. It still says "Every other entry keeps the renderer's generic icon". Each non-object kind now draws its `NAV_KIND_ICON` glyph on the neutral tile. This comment ships in the layout d.ts.
- N2. `CONTENT_KIND_ICON` (`contentItemTile.tsx`, lines 29 to 35) restates the `dashboard`, `report` and `page` glyphs of `NAV_KIND_ICON` instead of spreading them from `@object-ui/layout`. Two copies of "one rule" can drift.
- N3. On Home, an object, view or record row whose object is still `unread` (or was not found) draws the neutral tile with its kind glyph, then turns into the object tile once the read lands. In the same state, the sidebar's `ContentItemTile` draws the object tile (grey) from the start. One entry, two looks, for that window.
- N4. An app favourite (`app:NAME`, `type: 'object'`) in the Home-arm Starred list falls to the neutral tile with the fallback `file` glyph, because `CONTENT_KIND_ICON` has no `object` key. Not drawing it as an object tile is correct, but the app's own icon or a grid glyph would read better than a page.
- N5. A view favourite passes its stored `icon` (the object's icon when it was starred) ahead of the live object icon. A changed object icon therefore does not reach that row, while its colour does. This was already the behaviour before the PR.
- N6. `object-icon-tile-35985.test.tsx` says the neutral background is "lighter than every palette square" but compares it only with `gray-500`. The claim holds, but the test does not prove it as worded.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `5c70f68e51aa16ab58836ebda93cd22ba0201f5b`
Local-runs: none

This is a delta over the PASS record on `eb36a39789d71df8bdd5a5c948d6e34fae449ac2`. The new head is one commit over that one, `5c70f68e`, "fix(ui): sidebar Recent and Favorites ask their objects in one presence read". The merge base is still `f5553525`. Read: the delta diff `eb36a397..5c70f68e` (7 files, +123 / -60), the code it calls on the head (`readObjectPresence` in `console/appObjectScope.ts`, and `readObjectScope` in `providers/MetadataProvider.tsx`), the app-shell package entry, and the check-runs on the head. Of 66 check-runs, 54 are `success` and 12 `skipped`, and none failed. Every judgment of the earlier record not named below stands unchanged.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set: no change. The delta touches no `packages/spec` path, schema or validator.

Public surface:
- `@object-ui/layout`: only the jsdoc of `NavIconTarget` changes. It now says that every other entry draws its kind's icon (`NAV_KIND_ICON`) on the neutral tile, which matches the code. No declaration changes. This resolves N1.
- `@object-ui/components`: only a test changes. No surface change.
- `@object-ui/app-shell` (private): `readRecentObjects` and `RecentObjectReading` move, word for word, from `console/home/HomePage.tsx` to the new `console/home/readRecentObjects.ts`, and `HomePage.tsx` re-exports both. The package entry (`src/index.ts`) exports only `HomePage` and `DefaultHomePage` from that module, before and after, so the entry's surface is identical. Being private, the package has no published surface in any case. No surface change: right.
- `ContentItemTile` gains an optional `objectRead` prop, default `true`. It is internal to app-shell and not exported from the entry.
- `CONTENT_KIND_ICON` now spreads `NAV_KIND_ICON` and adds `package` and `metadata`. The `dashboard`, `report` and `page` values are unchanged, and the spread also brings in the other four kinds, so one table drives both. This resolves N2.

S1, judged against the code:
- `UnifiedSidebar` collects the object names of every favourite (`favoriteItemObject`) and of the five Recent rows it draws (`recentItemObject`). It de-duplicates and sorts them, then calls `readRecentObjects(metadata, names)` once per render.
- While the registry is `idle`, that call goes through `readObjectPresence`. That is ONE `readObjectScope` call with `views: false` and `batch: true`, the `GET /meta/object?names=` read, which leaves an absent name out instead of answering it 404. The batched scope asks only the names not asked yet, so Home's presence read and the sidebar's share the same request where their names overlap.
- `contentTile` passes `objectRead` only when the reading is `read`. On `unread` or `absent`, `ContentItemTile` returns the grey object tile before it calls `targetIcon` or `targetColor`, so no by-name read starts for that object.
- On `read`, the by-name scope answers from the presence read's own definition (objectstack#35306), so no second request is made.
- Once the whole registry is loaded or loading, the function answers from that list, as Home does.
- The new pin, `UnifiedSidebar.favoritesMenu-12427.test.tsx`, is the last case of the 36141 describe. With the registry `idle`, it asserts that every batched call names exactly `account` and `crm_deal`. It also asserts that no non-batched call names the missing `crm_deal`, and that the missing object's row is the grey object tile while the present one is teal.
- Without the gate, `useNavTargetIcon` would call `readObjectsByName`, a non-batched names-only call naming `crm_deal`, so the pin fails as claimed.
- S1 is resolved.

Unchanged judgments re-checked on this head: items 1-3 and 5-7, the favourite id formats, and the widening that the PR body and changeset name.

### ② Semver level

There is no change. The changeset is not in the delta and still bumps components, layout and app-shell at `patch`. The delta adds no published export and no public declaration; the one public change is a jsdoc line. `Metadata-protocol: none` and `Clause-②: yes (widening)` still match the net diff against `main`. That is right under ruling A.

### ③ Boundary flags

SQL push-down: no finding. The delta replaces per-name metadata reads with one batched presence read, which is the direction Prime Directive 5 asks for. It adds no data query, id materialisation or in-app join.

Must-fix: none.

Should-fix: none open. S1 is resolved, as above.

Nits:
- N1, N2 and N6 are resolved. N6: the pin now compares the light neutral background with the light shade of every name in `OBJECT_COLORS`.
- N3 is still open and now explicit: for an object row that is `unread` or `absent`, Home draws the neutral tile with its kind glyph, while the sidebar draws the grey object tile.
- N4 is still open: an app favourite in the Starred list draws the fallback `file` glyph.
- N5 is still open: a view favourite's stored icon goes ahead of the live object icon.
- N7, new: the `export { readRecentObjects, type RecentObjectReading }` in `HomePage.tsx` has no importer on the head. Home and the sidebar both import from `./readRecentObjects.js`. The re-export is harmless, but it could be dropped.
- Observation, outside this PR: the sidebar's Recent label reader (`useRecentItemLabel`, its `listTitle` arm) still reads an `object` or `view` row's object by name with no presence gate. That is `main`'s behaviour, unchanged by this PR; Home gates the same reader through `labelRecent`. It is worth a card if the 34692 rule is meant to cover the whole sidebar.

Reviewed-by: `session_01L6bhgUkbQqRUUFSiu2HGob (isolated L2 sub-agent of the seat)`

**VERDICT: PASS**
